feed.title: Combined summary - Propagation Delay and Mining Centralization: Modeling Stale Rates

entry.title: Combined summary - Propagation Delay and Mining Centralization: Modeling Stale Rates
entry.summary: Selfish mining is a sophisticated strategy within the Bitcoin network that enables certain miners to enhance their earnings by timing the publication of newly found blocks rather than adhering strictly to standard protocol. This approach is particularly advantageous for miners or pools with significant hashrate, as longer block propagation times can create race conditions in which larger players are statistically more likely to succeed. The phenomenon has been examined using simplified models that assume uniform propagation delay and immediate miner responses upon block discovery. In such idealized conditions, a miner’s revenue aligns proportionally with its share of network hashrate. However, real-world delays introduce the risk of blocks becoming stale—effectively invalid—if competing blocks reach the majority of miners first. Two main scenarios arise: one in which a rival miner discovers a block before others, causing the network to migrate toward the new chain tip; and another where quick successive block discoveries heighten the likelihood of staleness. Larger mining entities, due to their control over more substantial portions of the hashrate, are better positioned to win these time-sensitive races, leading to increased centralization. Simulations leveraging current hashrate distributions reveal how even minor differences in propagation speed can dramatically affect stale rates and, consequently, pool revenues. Such findings highlight the critical need for miners to carefully select pools based on size and responsiveness, while also emphasizing the broader significance of network improvements that reduce propagation delays to promote decentralization and fairness. For those seeking technical depth, comprehensive data analysis can be explored through resources like the [detailed analysis of Selfish Mining](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/where-does-the-33-33-threshold-for-selfish-mining-come-from/1757) and the corresponding simulation code hosted on [GitHub](https://github.com/darosior/miningsimulation/blob/d10b4346cf15eb6cda198414702b64fe685754fa/plot_stale_rate/plot.py). Financial realities in mining are much more nuanced than headline revenue numbers suggest. A large percentage of gross revenue—often cited at figures around $91 million—is consumed by operational expenses, particularly electricity costs. This means that net profits are highly sensitive to small changes in revenue streams. For example, a seemingly negligible decrease of 0.05% in revenue could slash profits by as much as 5%, illustrating the razor-thin margins under which many mining operations function. These economic pressures further accentuate the competitive dynamics introduced by propagation delays and stale blocks. Network protocol developments are underway to address technical challenges surrounding the management and visibility of stale blocks. One innovative proposal is the introduction of a "STALEHEADER" message type, which would allow nodes to relay headers near the blockchain’s tip without committing to serve entire blocks. This mechanism aims to improve network efficiency, particularly in the wake of compact block implementation, by providing better statistics on near-tip staleness and invalid forks while safeguarding against denial-of-service attacks through sensible activation requirements. The concept, being developed under initiatives like Chaincode's BOSS project, requires careful integration, as it must balance performance benefits with network security and resilience. The evolution of benchmarking tools and protocols plays a central role in advancing blockchain ecosystems. The Stratum Protocol exemplifies this progress by offering a robust framework designed to tackle core challenges such as transaction throughput, consensus efficiency, and cross-chain interoperability. Through the use of advanced cryptography and optimized networking, Stratum enhances transaction speeds, reduces latency, and upholds high standards of security and privacy. Its capacity to facilitate seamless interaction between disparate blockchain systems is pivotal for fostering an integrated ecosystem, supporting both decentralized application development and regulatory compliance. Developers interested in leveraging these capabilities can access resources and documentation at the [Stratum Protocol Blog](https://stratumprotocol.org/blog/hashlabs), which provides essential guidance for implementing and extending the protocol within diverse projects. Within the ongoing enhancement of Bitcoin's protocol, the community has seen the drafting of a new Bitcoin Improvement Proposal ([BIP draft](https://github.com/ajtowns/bips/blob/f25fa67b03fc0ebbf994aca62d96c1990da8fd9d/bip-staletip.md)) and its associated [vibe-coded implementation](https://github.com/ajtowns/bitcoin/tree/202601-staletips-vibes). These efforts represent proactive steps toward refining the mechanisms governing stale block handling and improving network reliability. Although the proposal remains untested with live data, it offers a blueprint for future development and invites scrutiny, testing, and collaborative feedback from the open-source community. Discussions regarding whether to propagate full stale blocks or only their headers reflect the continuous balancing act between innovation and operational efficiency within protocol design. Recent updates to mining simulation methodologies underscore the importance of presenting miner revenue changes not merely as raw shares of discovered blocks but as proportional shifts relative to each miner’s baseline.
